messages:
Incident Bot: [ALERT] Service degradation detected for customer Harbor Corp (VPC - dedicated pool 'harbor-west') in us-west-2. Elevated 5xx and proxy timeouts reported.
Jamie SRE: ack. paging @Neha and @Lucas. grabbing logs and current pool state.
Neha Patel: on it, pulling metrics from the dedicated fleet. ETA ~3m.
Lucas M.: quick glance — GPU mem pressure on harbor-west-primary hit 95% and kernel OOM evictions started; KV cache thrashing likely. Seeing p50 latency spike to 750ms and 502s from the proxy.
Mike D.: I'm starting to warm the standby pool (harbor-west-warm-01). Allocating 4x A100, setting autoscale min to 4.
Carlos (Harbor): we have support tickets coming in — some customers seeing generation failures. Any mitigation ETA?
Jamie SRE: propose a graceful weighted traffic shift to the warm pool + TTL reduction on tenant DNS to minimize client cache time. Plan: 1) drop DNS TTL to 30s, 2) apply weighted routing (primary=10,warm=90), 3) drain primary. Comments? @Carlos want you aware before we change routing. :point_up: 
Neha Patel: lowering TTL on harbor.company.com to 30s now via infra-dns. Change ID change-5863.
Lucas M.: ready to apply weighted route. Command I'll run from ops jumpbox:
```
redwood route update --tenant harbor --region us-west-2 --weights primary=10,warm-01=90
```
Jamie SRE: executing the route update now.
Incident Bot: Action initiated by Jamie SRE at 1768123500: route update submitted.
Incident Bot: Action result: SUCCESS. New routing weights applied: primary=10%, warm-01=90%.
Mike D.: warm pool healthchecks passing: p50=42ms, p95=120ms, 0 5xx in the last 30s.
Carlos (Harbor): confirming session stickiness — will cookies work across pools? We have sticky sessions for some customers.
Lucas M.: yes — we added a migration header and fallback. New sessions should land on warm pool; existing sticky tokens will continue for a short window. We'll flush KV on primary before full shutdown to avoid stale responses.
Jamie SRE: initiating drain on the primary pool to stop new sessions from being accepted:
```
redwood pool drain --pool harbor-west-primary --timeout 300
```
Neha Patel: drain started. Active connections dropping 420 -> 180 -> 60.
Jamie SRE: monitoring errors and customer tickets. If 5xx stays low we keep warm pool as active for at least 1 hour.
(5 minutes pass)
Incident Bot: Auto-alert: 5xx rate decreasing, system-level errors back within baseline.
Carlos (Harbor): seeing a big drop in failed requests. Thanks team. Can you keep warm capacity for 2 hours while we watch?
Mike D.: affirmative — keeping warm-01 up for +2h and setting autoscale min to preserve capacity. Billing note: reserve capacity is in effect.
Jamie SRE: putting short notes for post-incident: root cause looks like KV eviction due to under-provisioned memory for harbor workload; autoscale didn't trigger fast enough because of burst pattern. Immediate mitigation: weighted shift + TTL drop + warm pool. Medium-term: increase KV sizing for tenant, tune eviction policy, and adjust autoscale threshold.
Lucas M.: adding a quick config snippet we applied to routing so it's reproducible:
```
# routing change applied
tenant: harbor
region: us-west-2
weights:
  primary: 10
  warm-01: 90
```
Neha Patel: starting incident doc and assigning owners. I'll take lead on PMing the postmortem.
Jamie SRE: handing off monitoring and postmortem to Neha for overnight. Everyone: if new errors spike, page the oncall and re-open this thread.
Neha Patel: taking over. I'll own remediation (KV sizing + autoscale tuning) and coordinate with customer success for a follow-up meeting.
Lucas M.: owners noted: Neha (lead postmortem), Mike (infra & warm pool ops), Jamie (support & playbook), Lucas (routing & KV analysis).
Incident Bot: Incident RESOLVED at 1768123799. Summary: Weighted traffic shift to warm pool + TTL reduction mitigated 5xx surge triggered by KV cache eviction on primary dedicated pool. Postmortem required and owners assigned.
Jamie SRE: closing the active ops loop. :white_check_mark: We'll recommend a 20% headroom for dedicated tenant pools and a playbook update for automatic warm-pool promotion.
Carlos (Harbor): very grateful for the quick response. Please loop in our TAM for the postmortem.
Neha Patel: will do — starting the incident write-up and scheduling a follow-up with Harbor TAM.
